authority: Programme Officer at the Block (Panchayat at intermediate level), for disputes about implementation by the Gram Panchayat
portal_name: No online portal at this rung — written complaint to the Block Programme Officer
description: Hand in a written, dated complaint at the Block office addressed to the Programme Officer — s.23(5) sends Gram Panchayat disputes to him and s.23(6) obliges him to enter every complaint in a complaint register and dispose of it within seven days, so insist on a receipt showing the register entry number.

authority: District Programme Coordinator — the Chief Executive Officer of the District Panchayat or the District Collector (s.14)
portal_name: MGNREGA Public Grievance Redressal — online 'Lodge Complaint' (state-wise)
description: Open this page, click your State, and the State's MGNREGA complaint form loads (it asks for complaint type, complaint source, district, block and Gram Panchayat, and the details of the complaint) — the District Programme Coordinator is the officer accountable for implementation in the district under s.14.

authority: MGNREGA Ombudsperson for your district
portal_name: MGNREGA Ombudsperson (district-level, complaints accepted electronically or on paper)
description: Every district is meant to have an Ombudsperson who receives MGNREGA grievances, issues a dated receipt as soon as the complaint is received, and passes awards — find their name and mobile number on the Citizen Information Board in your Gram Panchayat or ask at the Block/District office, because the Ministry publishes no national directory.

authority: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
portal_name: CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System)
description: Register an account on CPGRAMS (it now accepts grievances only from registered users) and lodge against the Ministry of Rural Development, keeping the registration number to track it; if the closure is unsatisfactory, rate it 'Poor' to unlock the appeal.

authority: Executive Engineer / Head of the Programme Implementation Unit (PIU) for your district
portal_name: PMGSY District Programme Implementation Unit (written complaint)
description: Send a written complaint about quality of works to the Head of the PIU for your district — para 15.8 names the Head of PIU as an authority empowered to receive and enquire into complaints and requires a reply after proper investigation within 30 days; quote the road name, length and contractor exactly as printed on the site signboard required by para 11.4.

authority: State Quality Coordinator (SQC), State Rural Roads Development Agency (SRRDA)
portal_name: State Quality Coordinator (contact details publicised by the State)
description: The SQC is the officer formally empowered to receive quality complaints and para 15.8(i) requires each State to publicise the SQC's name and address; the SQC must register your complaint, give you a registration number and a likely reply date, have it enquired into by the PIU or a State Quality Monitor, and reply within 30 days with the action taken.

authority: National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (NRIDA/NRRDA), Ministry of Rural Development
portal_name: Meri Sadak (citizen feedback — mobile app only, no web form)
description: Meri Sadak is the dedicated citizen complaint channel for PMGSY roads and exists only as a mobile app linked from the official PMGSY portal — there is no web filing form; complaints already filed can be browsed by state/district/block at https://pmgsy.dord.gov.in/Feedback/QueryFeedBack/StateFeedBackLayout.

authority: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
portal_name: CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System)
description: Register and file against the Ministry of Rural Development, keeping the registration ID; para 15.8(v) says complaints received through the Ministry/NRRDA are normally sent to the State Quality Coordinator for enquiry, and NRRDA may depute a National Quality Monitor if the State does not respond adequately in time.

authority: Village revenue official / Patwari and the Block Agriculture Officer who verify land records and upload beneficiary data
portal_name: PM-KISAN portal — Beneficiary Status and 'Update Missing Information' self-service
description: Pull your own record from the PM-KISAN portal first so you can quote the exact failure reason, then take it in writing to the village revenue official and the Block Agriculture Officer, who are the people who actually enter and correct your land and Aadhaar details.

authority: PM-KISAN Help Desk, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
portal_name: PM-KISAN Helpdesk — Grievance Query Form
description: Raise the grievance on the scheme's own online query form, which issues a Grievance ID and date you can quote later, and which also carries an appeal option once a reply is recorded.

authority: State Nodal Officer for PM-KISAN and the District Level Grievance Redressal Monitoring Committee
portal_name: PM-KISAN — searchable State Nodal Officer contact directory
description: Each State designates a nodal department and a State Nodal Officer for PM-KISAN — look yours up in this official searchable directory and escalate there, since para 7.2 puts the State and District Grievance Redressal Monitoring Committees in charge of scheme grievances.

authority: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
portal_name: CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System)
description: If the scheme helpdesk and the State nodal officer both fail you, register on CPGRAMS and lodge against the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, keeping the registration number to track and appeal.

authority: Designated PMAY-G grievance official at Gram Panchayat / Block level (Block Development Officer or the official designated by the State)
portal_name: PMAY-G grievance official designated for your Gram Panchayat/Block (written complaint)
description: Hand in a written complaint to the PMAY-G grievance official designated for your Gram Panchayat or Block — para 12.3 requires their name, telephone number and address to be displayed in every Panchayat, and para 12.2 gives them 15 days to dispose of it; first pull your own sanction and instalment record from AwaasSoft at https://awaassoft.pmayg.dord.gov.in/netiay/Benificiary.aspx so you can quote dates and amounts.

authority: Three-member District Appellate Committee headed by the District Magistrate/Collector (wait-list grievances); designated district-level grievance official (all other complaints)
portal_name: District Appellate Committee / DRDA
description: If your complaint is about deletion from the list or a change in your ranking, submit it during the 15-day window that opens after the list has been publicised for seven days — to the Competent Authority (the BDO or state-designated official), who must enquire and send a report to the District Appellate Committee headed by the Collector, which decides the appeal (paras 4.5.2-4.5.3).

authority: State-level designated PMAY-G grievance official, State Rural Development Department
portal_name: CPGRAMS — State Government Nodal Public Grievance Officers directory
description: Para 12.1 requires a designated grievance official at State level as well as Gram Panchayat, Block and District; if the Block and District rungs have not answered within 15 days each, escalate in writing to the State Rural Development Department, using this official state-wise directory of nodal public grievance officers to find the right desk.

authority: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
portal_name: CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System)
description: Register an account and file against the Ministry of Rural Development, keeping the registration ID — para 12.4 requires complaints reaching the Ministry to be forwarded to your State, which must send an Action Taken Report within one month under intimation to you; if the reply is unsatisfactory, rate it 'Poor' to unlock the appeal option.

authority: Gram Panchayat and its water sub-committee — Village Water & Sanitation Committee (VWSC) / Paani Samiti / User Group
portal_name: Gram Panchayat / VWSC (Paani Samiti) — in person; no online complaint portal exists at this rung
description: Give a written complaint to the Sarpanch or Panchayat Secretary, or raise it in the Gram Sabha — under JJM the Gram Panchayat/VWSC is responsible for managing, operating and maintaining the in-village water supply system, so this is the first and fastest stop.

authority: District Water and Sanitation Mission (DWSM), headed by the District Collector / Deputy Commissioner, with the Executive Engineer PHED / Rural Water Supply as Member-Secretary
portal_name: District Water & Sanitation Mission (DWSM) — District Collectorate / PHED division office
description: If the Panchayat cannot fix it, submit a written complaint to the District Collector's office addressed to the DWSM, or to the Executive Engineer of the PHED/RWS division — 'grievance redressal' is an explicitly listed DWSM function (Operational Guidelines para 5.3 item xxvii, printed p.31).

authority: State Water and Sanitation Mission (SWSM) — headed by the Chief Secretary, with the Secretary in charge of PHED / Rural Water Supply as Mission Director
portal_name: Your own State's PHED / Rural Water Supply Department or State JJM portal (each State runs its own)
description: Rural water supply is a State subject, so escalate to your own State's PHED/Rural Water Supply Department or State Jal Jeevan Mission — there is no single national index of State portals, so use the CPGRAMS State Government nodal-officer directory to reach the right State grievance machinery.

authority: National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti
portal_name: CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System)
description: Lodge the grievance on CPGRAMS choosing Ministry of Jal Shakti then Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, quoting your village, Gram Panchayat, district and State; the number is the Office of the Mission Director, NJJM as printed in the footer of jaljeevanmission.gov.in — an office landline during working hours, not a 24x7 citizen helpline.

authority: Head Teacher and the School Management Committee (SMC) of the school
portal_name: School Management Committee — raised in person or in writing at the school (no online portal at this rung)
description: Raise the complaint in writing with the head teacher and the SMC — para 2.4 makes the SMC (constituted under the RTE Act, 2009) responsible for monitoring PM POSHAN implementation, meal quality, cleanliness of the cooking place and hygiene, and para 2.5(ii) gives it day-to-day management of the programme at school level.

authority: District Nodal Officer / District Nodal Agency for PM POSHAN — normally the District Collector, or the CEO of the District Panchayat where primary education is devolved
portal_name: Office of the District Nodal Officer / District Collectorate (no national online portal at this rung)
description: If the school does not fix it, send a written complaint to the district nodal officer for PM POSHAN — para 2.3 requires every State/UT to designate a nodal officer or agency at district and block level with overall responsibility, and makes the District Nodal Agency responsible for ensuring each school knows its monthly foodgrain allocation and financial sanction.

authority: State/UT PM POSHAN grievance redressal mechanism, run by the State Nodal Department/Officer
portal_name: State/UT PM POSHAN public grievance mechanism (varies by State — not published centrally)
description: Paras 11.1 and 15.7 require every State and UT to run a dedicated, widely publicised and easily accessible grievance mechanism for PM POSHAN 'like toll free call facility etc.' — ask the State education department or the district nodal officer for your State's PM POSHAN line, because the Centre publishes no national list of these numbers.

authority: Department of School Education & Literacy (PM POSHAN Division), Ministry of Education
portal_name: CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System)
description: Register on CPGRAMS and lodge the grievance against the Ministry of Education / Department of School Education & Literacy; you get a registration ID to track it, and if the closure is unsatisfactory you can rate it 'Poor' and appeal.

authority: Gram Panchayat / Ward Sabha, and the officer designated by the State for grievance redressal at Gram or Intermediate Panchayat level
portal_name: No online portal at this rung — written complaint to the Gram Panchayat / designated grievance officer
description: Hand in a written complaint at the Gram Panchayat or to the State-designated grievance officer and insist on a dated receipt stating the redressal timeline — para 6.9 makes that receipt mandatory, and para 3.4 entitles you to inspect the register of applications, sanction orders and rejections at that same office.

authority: District or Block level Welfare Officer (District Social Welfare Officer / BDO), and the Appellate Authority nominated by the State for the first appeal
portal_name: NSAP FAQ — official statement of whom to approach with a complaint
description: The NSAP FAQ (Question 36) states that the concerned District or Block level Welfare Officer can be approached for redressal of any complaint under NSAP; if your application was rejected, file the first appeal here — it must be disposed of within 15 days under para 3.5.

authority: State Nodal Secretary / State Nodal Department dealing with NSAP (Social Welfare or Rural Development, varies by State), and the Reviewing Authority for the second appeal
portal_name: CPGRAMS — State Government Nodal Public Grievance Officers directory
description: NSAP is delivered by your State, so this is the rung that actually controls your money — use this official directory to find your State's nodal grievance officer, since the NSAP FAQ (Question 36) names the State Nodal Secretary dealing with NSAP as a complaint authority and the second appeal also lies with a State-nominated Reviewing Authority under para 3.3.

authority: NSAP Division, Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development
portal_name: CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System)
description: The NSAP portal's own 'Grievance Redressal' menu links to CPGRAMS, so lodge the grievance online there (CPGRAMS warns that emailed grievances are not entertained); the phone number is the Economic Adviser, NSAP Division, printed on the official NSAP Contact Us page, which states 'For any NSAP related issues contact NSAP Division, MoRD' — it is a Delhi desk line, not a citizen helpline.

authority: State PDS call centre / helpline, and the Vigilance Committee at the fair price shop level
portal_name: Toll Free Helpline Numbers for PDS in States/UTs (Department of Food and Public Distribution)
description: Call the national PDS toll-free number 1967 or your State's own PDS helpline to register a complaint against the fair price shop — s.14 obliges every State to run this internal mechanism, and the official directory page lists the State/UT numbers.

authority: District Grievance Redressal Officer (DGRO) appointed under s.15, working out of the District Food and Supply Office
portal_name: District Food and Supply Offices directory (NFSA portal)
description: Take a written complaint about non-distribution of your entitled foodgrains to the District Grievance Redressal Officer — s.15(1) requires your State to appoint or designate one for every district specifically to enforce NFSA entitlements, and s.15(5) requires him to hear the complaint and act within the time prescribed by the State.

authority: State Food Commission (statutory appellate body under s.16)
portal_name: Online Grievance (State Portal) directory — NFSA portal
description: If the District Grievance Redressal Officer's order does not satisfy you, appeal to your State Food Commission under s.15(6) — it hears appeals against the DGRO under s.16(6)(e) and can inquire into entitlement violations on its own motion, with the powers of a civil court; PDS is run state by state, so use this directory to reach your own State's online grievance portal.

authority: Department of Food and Public Distribution, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
portal_name: NFSA Portal — Register your Grievance
description: Register the grievance on the national NFSA portal, and if it still is not resolved, escalate through CPGRAMS at https://pgportal.gov.in/Home/LodgeGrievance against the Department of Food and Public Distribution.

authority: Gram Panchayat — Sarpanch/Pradhan/Mukhiya and the Panchayat Secretary — through the Gram Sabha, supported by the Village Water & Sanitation Committee (VWSC)
portal_name: Gram Panchayat / Gram Sabha (in person — SBM-G has no online citizen complaint portal)
description: Raise it in the Gram Sabha and give a written complaint to the Sarpanch and Panchayat Secretary — eligible households are identified by the Gram Panchayat in the Gram Sabha (para 5.1), and a Social Audit meeting must be held in every Gram Panchayat once every six months (para 17.7), which is the guideline-backed moment to put a missing toilet, a missing payment or a false ODF Plus claim on record.

authority: Block Development Officer (heads the Block Water & Sanitation Committee), then the District Swachh Bharat Mission Grameen — the District Collector / CEO Zila Panchayat is the nodal officer
portal_name: Block Development Officer's office / District Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), with the public SBM(G) dashboard as evidence
description: Take a written complaint to the BDO (the Block Water & Sanitation Committee sits under the BDO and monitors asset quality and usage in every GP) and, if unresolved, to the District Collector as DSBM(G) nodal officer — attach the district's own reported figures printed on the public SBM(G) dashboard.

authority: State Mission SBM(G) / State Water and Sanitation Mission (SWSM), under the State's Rural Development / Panchayati Raj / PHED department
portal_name: Your own State's SBM(G) Mission or rural sanitation department (each State runs its own)
description: Rural sanitation is delivered by the State, so escalate to your State's SBM(G) Mission Directorate or SWSM — there is no national index of State SBM portals, so use the CPGRAMS State Government nodal-officer directory to find the right desk.

authority: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti
portal_name: CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System)
description: Lodge the grievance on CPGRAMS choosing Ministry of Jal Shakti then Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, quoting your village, Gram Panchayat, district and State; the SBM-G national site publishes only postal addresses for the Joint Secretary and Director (Sanitation) and no grievance phone number.

authority: Your Village Organisation (VO) and Cluster Level Federation (CLF), then the Block Mission Management Unit (BMMU) grievance cell
portal_name: No online portal at this rung — raise it in the SHG/VO/CLF meeting and in writing to the BMMU grievance cell
description: Raise the issue in your SHG meeting and get it minuted, escalate through the VO and CLF, then complain in writing to the Block Mission Management Unit grievance cell, which para 13.9 requires to be constituted and to maintain a record of complaints received, resolved and pending.

authority: District Mission Management Unit (DMMU) grievance cell, under the district administration
portal_name: No national online portal — written complaint to the DMMU grievance cell
description: If the block does not resolve it, complain in writing to the District Mission Management Unit grievance cell that para 13.9 requires every State Rural Livelihoods Mission to constitute; because the DMMU sits under the district administration, the District Collector's office is the practical backstop.

authority: State Rural Livelihoods Mission (SRLM) — State Mission Management Unit (SMMU) grievance cell
portal_name: CPGRAMS — State Government Nodal Public Grievance Officers directory (to locate your State's mission/department)
description: DAY-NRLM runs under your State's own brand (Rajeevika, Jeevika, Kudumbashree and so on) and para 13.9 requires an SMMU grievance cell — use this official directory to find your State's nodal grievance officer, because there is no single national DAY-NRLM grievance portal.

authority: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
portal_name: CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System)
description: Lodge the grievance online against the Ministry of Rural Development or your State's rural development department — CPGRAMS connects all Ministries, Departments and States, and explicitly warns that grievances sent by email are not entertained.

authority: Reserve Bank of India Ombudsman (Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme), Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre
portal_name: RBI Complaint Management System (CMS)
description: This is a separate track, not a rung above CPGRAMS: if the complaint is against a bank — SHG account or loan refused, wrong interest charged, interest subvention not credited — complain to the bank first, and if it does not resolve the matter file with the RBI Ombudsman on CMS; the 14448 contact centre with IVRS is available 24x7, with personnel reachable Monday to Saturday 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM in English, Hindi and ten regional languages.

authority: School Management Committee (SMC) of the school — at least three-fourths parents/guardians and 50% women
portal_name: School Management Committee — raised at the school (no online portal at this rung)
description: Raise the issue first with the head teacher and the SMC, which under RTE s.21(2) monitors the working of the school and the utilisation of its grants; note that under the proviso to s.21(2) the SMC is advisory only in minority-managed and aided schools.

authority: The 'local authority' with jurisdiction over the school — Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, Zila Parishad, Nagar Panchayat or Panchayat (RTE s.2(h))
portal_name: Written complaint to the local authority under RTE s.32(1) (no national online portal for this statutory step)
description: RTE s.32(1) lets any person with a grievance about a child's right under the Act make a written complaint to the local authority having jurisdiction, and s.32(2) requires that authority to decide within three months after hearing both sides — so file it in writing, dated, and keep an acknowledgement.

authority: State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (SCPCR), or the authority prescribed by the State Government under RTE s.31(3) where no SCPCR exists
portal_name: Appeal to the SCPCR under RTE s.32(3) (each State runs its own site — no verified national directory exists)
description: If the local authority's decision does not satisfy you, or it fails to decide, appeal to your State Commission for Protection of Child Rights under s.32(3); the SCPCR is independently empowered by s.31(1)(b) to inquire into complaints about a child's right to free and compulsory education.

authority: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), Ministry of Women and Child Development
portal_name: e-BaalNidaan — NCPCR Online Complaint Management System
description: Register the complaint online on e-BaalNidaan choosing 'Education' from the Complaint Head dropdown — NCPCR is empowered under RTE s.31(1)(b) to inquire into complaints about the right to free and compulsory education; use e-BaalNidaan and NOT the POCSO e-Box, which NCPCR restricts to child sexual abuse complaints.

authority: Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG), routing to any Ministry, Department, State or UT
portal_name: CPGRAMS — Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System
description: Create an account (grievances can now be lodged only by registered users), lodge the grievance against the right Ministry/Department or State, and keep the registration number — track it at https://pgportal.gov.in/Status; a grievance sent by email instead of the portal is not entertained.

authority: Appellate Authority of the department that closed your grievance (within CPGRAMS)
portal_name: CPGRAMS Appeal
description: If your grievance is closed and you are not satisfied, rate the resolution 'Poor' — that unlocks the appeal option against the original registration number, and the appeal is tracked at this URL.

authority: State/UT Nodal Public Grievance Officer
portal_name: CPGRAMS — State Government Nodal Public Grievance Officers directory
description: For any scheme actually delivered by a State (PDS, pensions, water, sanitation, school meals), this official state-wise directory is how you find the right State desk instead of guessing at 36 separate portals.

authority: Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) of the public authority holding the records
portal_name: RTI Online (Department of Personnel & Training)
description: File an RTI application online against any Central Government ministry, department or public authority — you need give no reason and no personal details beyond contact details (RTI Act s.6(2)), the fee is the amount prescribed in the RTI Rules 2012 and is waived for BPL applicants who attach their certificate, and the CPIO must answer within 30 days (48 hours where life or liberty is at stake) under s.7(1). The helpline 011-24010690/691 operates 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM, Monday to Friday.

authority: First Appellate Authority — the officer senior in rank to the CPIO in the same public authority
portal_name: RTI Online — Submit First Appeal
description: If you get no reply within 30 days or you are unhappy with the reply, file a first appeal within 30 days under RTI Act s.19(1) — no fee is payable for a first appeal.

authority: Central Information Commission (for Central public authorities) or your State Information Commission
portal_name: Central Information Commission
description: A second appeal lies to the Central Information Commission (or the State Information Commission for State public authorities) within 90 days of the date the first-appeal decision should have been or was made, under RTI Act s.19(3); the burden of proving that a denial was justified is on the PIO, not on you.

authority: Your Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha)
portal_name: Sansad — Lok Sabha / Rajya Sabha member directories
description: Look up your MP by constituency or State in the official Lok Sabha directory (Rajya Sabha members at https://sansad.in/rs/members), then write to their office with your grievance and the scheme reference/registration number — an MP's letter to a Ministry or Collector is a real escalation route and MPs can raise the matter in Parliament.
